item.title: Kevin Warsh Delivers a ‘Perplexing’ Fed Briefing, and Gets a Bronx Cheer
item.description: The Fed kept interest rates unchanged, causing investors to dump 30-year Treasury bonds.

item.title: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg Fails to Fill In The Details on an AI Cloud Business
item.description: Investors and analysts are still waiting for the Meta CEO to give details of a new AI business

item.title: BOE Holds Rates in Split Vote as War Clouds Inflation Outlook
item.description: The Bank of England kept interest rates steady at 3.75%, as UK officials sought to balance the threat from resurgent US-Iran tensions against signs that domestic price pressures are easing more quickly than predicted.

item.title: Lighthizer and Trump tariffs
item.description: In a new podcast, the architect of Trump’s first-term tariff agenda says things are progressing just fine

item.title: Labcorp Raises Earnings Outlook on Strong Medical Testing Demand
item.description: Labcorp Holdings Inc. raised its outlook for the year after reporting second-quarter earnings that topped analyst estimates, citing strength in cancer tests and new genetic screenings.

item.title: Britain Saw Limited Non-Dom Exits Ahead of Tax Reforms Last Year
item.description: The number of wealthy foreign residents in the UK claiming preferential tax treatment on their overseas earnings declined slightly in the final fiscal year before the country ended the special regime in April 2025.

item.title: Treasuries Extend Drop as Bond Traders Await Key Inflation Print
item.description: Treasuries extended their slide as traders braced for US inflation data that could cement concerns the Federal Reserve is dragging its feet on price growth.

item.title: Pakistan Secures Safe Passage for LNG Shipment With Iran Deal
item.description: Pakistan has negotiated with Iran to secure safe passage for at least one Qatari liquefied natural gas shipment, according to people with knowledge of the matter, the latest effort by the South Asian nation to use its diplomatic ties to ease a deepening energy crunch.

item.title: Traders Are Doubting Warsh’s Resolve on Inflation
item.description: Markets flash concern that the Fed won’t manage to rein in price pressures.

item.title: Why AI Is Making Cheap Flights Harder to Find
item.description: Airlines can now price seats with dynamic precision, closing pricing gaps that travelers loved.

item.title: Yuan Rises to Highest Since Early 2023 as Dollar Drops After Fed
item.description: The yuan strengthened to its highest level in more than three years against the dollar, buoyed by the renewed weakness in the US currency and continued policy support from Chinese authorities.

item.title: Disney CEO D'Amaro Wants to Overhaul Disney+ Streaming to Compete With Netflix
item.description: Streaming has been a drag on Disney’s share price as subscriber growth stalled. A tech overhaul and more foreign-language shows are in the cards.

item.title: SocGen Nears $5 Billion-Linked SRT Including Data Center Debt
item.description: Societe Generale SA is hedging about $5 billion of project finance deals by taking advantage of sustained investor demand for significant risk transfers.

item.title: CityFibre Said to Raise £900 Million to Challenge BT’s Openreach
item.description: CityFibre Ltd., the UK’s largest independent fiber challenger to incumbent BT Group Plc’s Openreach, is set to raise £900 million ($1.2 billion) from its shareholders, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: Credit Buyers Seek Refuge in Short-Dated Debt to Dodge Rate Risk
item.description: Investors are embracing shorter-term corporate debt, locking in elevated yields while limiting their exposure to interest-rate volatility and market swings.

item.title: Danantara Dollar Debt Plan Grapples With Global Bond Volatility
item.description: Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara’s planned dollar notes are unlikely to price quickly as a global bond rout clouds debt issuance, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Korean ETF Manager Urges Phase-Out of Leveraged Products
item.description: Bae Jae Kyu, the chief of South Korea’s sixth biggest asset manager, urged investors to refrain from trading leveraged and inverse exchange-traded funds, saying such products should be left to fade out.

item.title: Apple’s Earnings Will Test Stock’s Status as the AI Safety Play
item.description: Wall Street’s sudden aversion to AI spending has made Apple Inc. this year’s Big Tech stock market star. But the iPhone maker’s earnings after the close Thursday could remind investors of the hurdles it still faces.

item.title: Zambia’s Inflation Rate Holds Steady, Helped by Kwacha Strength
item.description: Zambia’s annual inflation rate held steady, remaining near the floor of the central bank’s 6% to 8% target range as a rally in the kwacha contained import costs.

In the decades since, Iran’s economy completely transformed, and it is closer to what Yeganeh Torbati and Bozorgmehr Sharafedin describe as a “mafia state,” where fealty to various factions is baked into the country’s political economy. item.title: US-Iran Talks ‘Ongoing’ to Normalize Situation, Pakistan Says
item.description: The negotiations between the US and Iran are “ongoing” to restore stability, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, Pakistan’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said at a weekly briefing in Islamabad.

item.title: Foxtons Sales Fees Drop 13% Showing London Housing Rut
item.description: Foxtons Group Plc has seen revenue from advising on home sales plunge, the latest sign of the downturn gripping the London housing market.

item.title: INR/USD: India Central Bank Sold About $7 Billion to Defend Rupee on Friday
item.description: India’s central bank sold about $7 billion to defend the rupee last Friday, in what was one of its largest direct interventions in months, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Saudi Economy Shrinks Most Since 2020 as War Roils Oil Exports
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s economy saw its sharpest quarterly contraction since the Covid-19 pandemic, as the US-Israeli war against Iran poses challenges to the vital oil industry.

item.title: LSEG Boosts Guidance as AI Rollout Adds to Record First Half
item.description: London Stock Exchange Group Plc raised its guidance for the year and said its push into artificial intelligence was gaining momentum with customers.

item.title: Anglo Cashes In on Copper as Strategy Shift Starts to Pay Off
item.description: Anglo American Plc saw a steep jump in earnings, driven by the copper mines that it’s put at the center of its new strategy.

item.title: Rolls-Royce Lifts Outlook Again as Demand Soars for Engines
item.description: Rolls-Royce Holdings Plc raised its full-year guidance for a second time as the UK’s largest manufacturer earned more from selling engines for widebody planes, military hardware and artificial intelligence.

item.title: Shell Profit Surges to $9.8 Billion on Oil Trading and Refining Gains
item.description: Shell Plc said its second-quarter profit soared to the highest since the outbreak of the Ukraine war as conflict in the Middle East drives a boom in trading and refining for the world’s energy majors.

item.title: Fed Doubts Push Some Funds to Eye Other Markets Over Treasuries
item.description: Some global bond investors are looking to shift toward markets like Australia and Europe as doubts grow over the Federal Reserve’s ability to keep inflation under control, adding to pressure on Treasuries.
